macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: US stocks rebound as oil retreats and chip shares recover
items.summary: U.S. stock index futures and broader markets rebounded as oil prices eased, helping investors look past some of the geopolitical pressure tied to U.S.-Iran tensions. Reuters also reported that Asian shares climbed and European shares gained, with technology stocks leading the recovery.

items.title: Oil volatility remains a key macro driver after fresh strikes in Iran
items.summary: Markets were still being driven by oil and inflation concerns after fresh U.S. strikes on Iran reignited anxiety over supply disruptions and the Strait of Hormuz. Reuters said oil prices rose on the renewed conflict, while Bloomberg noted Asian stocks were poised to drop as the selloff in chipmakers spread across markets.

items.title: Central banks stay focused on inflation risks amid supply shocks
items.summary: The Financial Times reported that some Fed officials saw a need for future rate rises to contain inflation, while Bloomberg quoted an RBA official warning that the world is likely to see more supply shocks and reinforcing the need to prioritize low and stable inflation. Reuters also reported that India’s inflation likely moved above the RBI’s 4% target in June.

items.title: Global growth outlook is being revised lower as war-related energy shock hits sentiment
items.summary: Al Jazeera reported that the IMF cut its 2026 global growth forecast, citing fallout from the Iran war, while still noting that AI demand partly offsets the energy shock. The same Reuters feed highlighted rising inflation pressure in several major economies, including China and India.

items.title: Japan bond yields hit a 30-year high as inflation concerns rise
items.summary: Reuters said the benchmark 10-year Japanese government bond yield hit a 30-year high as higher oil prices revived inflation concerns and investors worried about Japan’s fiscal health. Bloomberg also reported that Japan’s bank lending grew at the fastest pace since the Covid pandemic, supporting the case that the Bank of Japan has room to keep raising rates.

items.title: US market closes higher, with chip strength offsetting Iran worries
items.summary: Marketscreener reported that U.S. stocks ended higher, with a surge in chip shares offsetting concerns tied to Iran and the oil shock. Its 24-hour market snapshot showed the S&P 500 up 0.81% and the Nasdaq 100 up 1.62%.

items.title: Meta to start AI chip production in September
items.summary: MarketScreener reported that Meta Platforms aims to begin AI chip production in September, part of the broader push by large tech firms to expand computing capacity. The update was one of the most mentioned company developments over the past 24 hours.

items.title: Samsung begins mass production tied to Nvidia’s next data center platform
items.summary: Bloomberg reported that Samsung Electronics has begun mass production of its most advanced data center storage drive, which is set for use inside Nvidia’s upcoming Vera Rubin platform. The announcement adds to ongoing investor focus on AI infrastructure spending.

items.title: OPEC+ agrees to a modest August output increase
items.summary: Yahoo Finance reported that seven countries in the OPEC+ alliance agreed to lift combined oil output by 188,000 barrels per day in August. The move adds supply even as crude prices remain sensitive to the Iran-related disruption.

items.title: US economic growth and jobs data point to a softer backdrop
items.summary: A YouTube report said U.S. economic growth slowed in the second quarter of 2026, while the Financial Times reported that U.S. jobs added in June undershot forecasts at 57,000. Together, the releases point to slower momentum in the U.S. economy.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Meta releases Muse Spark 1.1 and launches Meta Model API
items.summary: Meta reportedly released Muse Spark 1.1 with improved coding capabilities and made it available to U.S. developers in a public API preview. The company also launched a Meta Model API, with Mark Zuckerberg describing pricing as about 25% of OpenAI and Anthropic's models.

items.title: OpenAI broadly releases GPT-5.6 and ChatGPT Work
items.summary: OpenAI reportedly broadened access to GPT-5.6 and introduced ChatGPT Work, an AI agent that can gather context across apps and files to create documents on Mac and Windows. Techmeme notes the release as a major product expansion in both model access and workplace automation.

items.title: Cognition releases SWE-1.7
items.summary: Cognition reportedly launched SWE-1.7, a model trained from Kimi K2.7 and available in Devin at 1,000 tokens per second. The company says it approaches frontier-level intelligence while reducing cost.

items.title: Ollama raises $65M Series B
items.summary: Ollama, the tool that helps developers run open-weight AI models locally, reportedly raised a $65 million Series B led by Theory Venture. The funding highlights continued investor demand for infrastructure that makes local model deployment easier.

items.title: Meta announces first data center in Canada
items.summary: Meta said it will build its first data center in Canada, a 1GW facility in Alberta expected to cost about $9 billion and take two to three years to construct. The announcement underscores the scale of infrastructure investment still driving AI expansion.

items.title: OpenAI faces scrutiny over AI evaluation reliability
items.summary: AIBase reported that OpenAI criticized benchmark quality, saying roughly 30% of 731 evaluation questions were flawed and that pass rates rose sharply over eight months, raising concerns about reliability. The item reflects ongoing debate over how to measure model progress credibly.

items.title: Google DeepMind researcher John Jumper reportedly leaving for Anthropic
items.summary: Reuters reported that John Jumper, a researcher at Google DeepMind, is set to leave for Anthropic. The move highlights continued competition for top AI talent among leading labs.

items.title: OpenAI CEO discussed upcoming models with lawmakers
items.summary: ABC News reported that Sam Altman met with lawmakers behind closed doors to discuss OpenAI's upcoming artificial intelligence models. The meeting comes amid broader government attention to AI controls and safety.

items.title: Gemini gets 'Personal Intelligence' feature
items.summary: Indian Express reported that Google added a 'Personal Intelligence' feature to Gemini, allowing the assistant to pull information from Gmail, Drive, and Photos. This points to a broader trend toward more deeply integrated personal AI assistants.

items.title: Industry trend: AI price competition intensifies
items.summary: Techmeme's roundup highlights aggressive pricing as a major theme, with Meta positioning its API around lower cost than OpenAI and Anthropic. That suggests the market is increasingly competing on price as well as model quality.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Palworld leaves early access and launches 1.0 today
items.summary: Palworld is officially out of early access, marking a major release milestone after reaching 40 million players, according to reporting from gaming news outlets. The launch is one of the day’s biggest game-release stories.

items.title: Buckshot Roulette launches on Xbox consoles and Game Pass
items.summary: Buckshot Roulette has just released on Xbox consoles and Xbox Game Pass, expanding the indie hit to a new platform audience. The release is one of the clearer same-day platform and subscription-service additions in the latest gaming coverage.

items.title: Mortal Shell II gets an August release window
items.summary: Mortal Shell II was announced with an August launch window for PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S. The announcement is notable as a new release update for a high-profile action RPG sequel.

items.title: Frostpunk 2 surpasses 1 million copies sold
items.summary: Frostpunk 2 has officially sold 1 million copies, making it one of the day’s notable industry success stories. The milestone underscores continued demand for premium strategy releases.

items.title: Mid-Season Invitational 2026 reaches the grand final stage
items.summary: Bilibili Gaming defeated Hanwha Life to secure the first spot in the MSI 2026 grand final. The result is a key esports development in one of the year’s major international League of Legends tournaments.

items.title: Ubisoft reportedly lays off 51 developers despite Black Flag success
items.summary: Coverage says Ubisoft is celebrating the success of Assassin’s Creed IV: Black Flag while also laying off 51 developers. The story is notable for the contrast between a franchise win and continued restructuring in the company.

items.title: PlayStation promotes a wireless fight stick after its disc-related tweet
items.summary: IGN reports that PlayStation followed up its recent tweet about killing discs by promoting a wireless fight stick, drawing attention for the company’s messaging around hardware and physical media. The post has become part of a broader discussion about PlayStation’s platform strategy.

items.title: Xbox Game Pass growth reportedly falls far short of Microsoft’s target
items.summary: IGN reports that Microsoft expected Game Pass to reach 77 million subscribers by now, but the service reportedly has only about 30 million, with Xbox leadership admitting the strategy has failed to grow as planned. This is one of the most significant industry-business stories in the latest coverage.
